correctness.rationale: For all finite abelian A=A₂⊕O and nonzero commutative unital rings K, basis [e_x,e_y]=e_{2y−x}−e_{2x−y}; the differences lie in 3A cosets and span their integral coefficient-sum kernels. Closure under bilinear quandle products gives full commutator-generated subalgebra B′=ker(K[A]→K[A/3A]). The fixed-factor image D=[−,e₀] is spanned by incidence edges e_x−e_{−2x}, hence componentwise sum-zero over any K. Functional components are indexed by −2-orbits on O, yielding free B′/im D≈K^{c(O)−|A/3A|}. This vanishes iff O is exponent 3, via distinct zero and nonzero orbits in the zero 3O coset otherwise. Telescoping σ=−2 produces an actual primitive when onto, proving fixed-factor and nontrivial width-one claims. Direct exact finite group evidence includes C9 obstruction rank2 and surjectivity for C2⊕C3⊕C3; finite samples corroborate, not replace, proof.
residual_risks: The fixed-factor condition is stricter than unrestricted commutator width; outside the onto family unrestricted width is not determined.
Free quotient claim relies on partition refinement giving a splitting, not just rank subtraction.

evidence: General Alexandrian ideal and core commutativization imply the coarse quotient A/3A, not its splitting into −2 orbits or fixed-factor surjectivity.
